summary:
SEMRA addresses these challenges through an offline-first, hybrid architecture. Because astronauts cannot rely on constant cloud access, the frontend runs as a standalone Progressive Web App with local storage and deterministic threshold rules, ensuring zero-latency vital tracking, SOS triggers, and step-by-step diagnostic checklists even when completely disconnected. When connected, it syncs crew profiles, medical baselines, and telemetry batches to Google Cloud Firestore and Ground Control.

Rather than using one-size-fits-all limits, SEMRA evaluates heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, radiation exposure, and biomarkers against each astronaut’s personal pre-flight baseline and current environment—dynamically adapting between onboard Spaceship mode and high-priority Outer Space (EVA) suit telemetry. Finally, it pairs instant rule-based safety flags with an AI Flight Surgeon powered by Gemini 2.5 Flash that cross-checks allergies and contraindications to generate actionable treatment plans, alongside daily workout and nutrition tracking to counter muscle and bone loss before emergencies happen.
details:
Space has no limits.

Our bodies do.

SEMRA is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and medical triage system built for deep-space missions where communication delays with Earth make real-time doctor consultations impossible.

How It Works & Benefits Crew members log in to track real-time telemetry (heart rate, blood pressure, O₂, temperature, radiation, ECG, and blood biomarkers) against their personal medical baselines. The app switches between Spaceship and Outer Space (EVA) modes, adapting alerts and interface layout to the astronaut’s environment. It combines an instant local rule engine with an AI Flight Surgeon (Gemini 2.5 Flash) to detect anomalies, cross-check allergies/contraindications, guide emergency diagnostics, manage personalized workout and nutrition plans, and sync logs with Ground Control when connectivity returns.

Intended Impact SEMRA gives astronauts immediate, life-saving clinical decision support during communication blackouts or high-latency missions to the Moon and Mars, while keeping Ground Control updated through automated batch syncing and structured log exports.

Tools & Technologies

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (React 18), Progressive Web App (Service Worker + offline LocalStorage caching)
  • Backend & Cloud: Python, FastAPI, Google Cloud Firestore, Google Cloud Storage, Vertex AI (Gemini 2.5 Flash)

Creativity & Team Considerations We designed SEMRA Offline-First because deep-space links drop or lag by up to 24 minutes. Instead of using generic medical thresholds, we tailored alerts to each astronaut’s pre-flight baseline, mission environment (cabin vs. EVA suit), and NASA Human Research Program hazards—combining deterministic safety rules with AI reasoning and gamified health habits to keep crews healthy and engaged on long missions.
